free_tier.stated: 'we've provided AWS Promotional Credits to more than 200 different open source projects' since the programme 'launched in 2019', and the credits 'can be used on compute resources, storage, database services, development tools, and testing infrastructure'. Applications are an Excel form emailed to the programme's own mailbox, reviewed and issued 'on a monthly basis', and 'The credits will expire after one year'.

egress.terms: 100 GB a month of data transfer out to the internet is free, aggregated across all AWS services and regions except China and GovCloud; the per-GB overage rate table is not in the page text read, so the overage price is unverified

interface_detail: a command-line tool, per the AWS CLI page: "The AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) is a unified tool to manage your AWS services."
tooling: the provider documents its own CLI, the AWS CLI, per https://aws.amazon.com/cli/: "The AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) is a unified tool to manage your AWS services."
chaining: Credits that cover 'compute resources, storage, database services' are the broadest instrument after a cash grant: the same balance pays for EC2 spot time, S3 and a managed database, so a whole pipeline runs on one award.

limits.value: An active AWS account with a valid payment method and no outstanding invoices is required before applying, review is monthly, and December issues no credits at all.

notes: The amount per project is not published on either AWS page, so the number is null; the two public figures are 200+ recipient projects and a one-year expiry, neither of which is a per-project size. Two eligibility lines tilt toward teams: 'not dominated by a single vendor' and a preference for maintainers from multiple entities, which is softer than Datadog's rule and does not exclude a solo maintainer outright. The 2019 post and the 2025 post give different application addresses (awsopen@ and [address removed]), so use the current form.
